Subject: Intermittent 5xx + latency spikes to Redwood endpoints

This is impacting our checkout flow; my CEO is pinging for an ETA. Please escalate.

Alex

Subject: Escalation: CobaltBridge prod latency — exec loop request

Team — pulling together the triage notes for CobaltBridge (CB-4521). Customer reports repeated latency/5xx spikes that coincide with an apparent throughput collapse. They indicated the CEO has begun asking for an ETA.

What we know so far:
- Errors coincide with elevated tail latency at our egress cluster in us-west-2 (observed ~14:58 and 15:10 PST).
- Initial logs show elevated SYN/ACK RTTs to the customer's VPC peer and a burst of DNS NXDOMAIN/timeout events to their resolver around the same time.
- No deploys from model infra teams in the last 3 hours.

Immediate asks:
- Vivek: Can you confirm any peering BGP flaps or route churn for peer pb-67 and whether NAT/session exhaustion is visible on the egress pool?
- Monica: Pull DNS resolver logs and proxy (squid/nginx) connection queue depth for the impacted nodes.
- Marissa: If this requires exec attention, recommend we loop in Eng leadership + our CRO for a customer brief.

I'll keep Alex updated with a 30-minute cadence.

Connor

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <ops@cobaltbridge.com>, Laura Chen <laura@cobaltbridge.com>, ceo@cobaltbridge.com
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Nov 2027 07:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: packet capture + SLA timeline (requested) — interim mitigation and findings

Alex / Laura — thanks for the pcap and timeline. Summary of what we found in the first-pass triage:
- BGP neighbor for peer pb-67 experienced a short-lived route withdrawal (approx 30s) at 14:58:12 PST followed by route re-announcement; several egress nodes showed a backlog in connection accept queues when the route flapped.
- We also observed a cluster of DNS timeouts from our resolver pool toward the customer's resolver IPs during the same second-range. This combination produced TCP retransmits and request timeouts at the application layer.
- The pcap shows retransmits with a TTL decrement consistent with traversal through a shared NAT hop (likely a third-party transit).

Interim mitigations we've applied (live now):
1) Expanded the egress pool for CobaltBridge routes to reduce per-node conntrack pressure (moved traffic to warm spare nodes).
2) Temporarily pinned routing to an alternate transit path (bypassing the flapping peer where possible) — this should reduce the immediate BGP churn exposure.
3) Increased DNS resolver retries and extended resolver timeout for CobaltBridge to hide transient resolver hiccups while we fix routing.

Effect: we see 90% reduction in 5xxs for the last 10 minutes and tail latency has improved (example request rb-req-67a3 succeeded at 07:12:08).

Next steps:
- We're coordinating with the transit provider to validate the shared NAT hop; I'll share their ticket id when available.
- We'll run a canary load for 30 minutes before we revert any temporary routing pins.
- Connor/Monica/Marissa will be on a 1-hour update cadence to you.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Prod Infra, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bC-pcap-logs (pcap + analysis)

Please keep the temporary mitigations in place until the transit provider confirms the NAT hop behavior. We'll expect the postmortem and the long-term fix plan (BGP hardening + DNS resolver redundancy) in 48 hours.

I'll leave the thread open for the postmortem.

Alex
